intro: A martial arts school sign makes a claim. It names an art, and often a founder, a style or a headquarters far away. Behind the sign stand older institutions: a Japanese scroll listing headmasters since the 1400s, a Tokyo registry of dan ranks begun in 1883, a Seoul headquarters opened in 1972, or a Brazilian family academy opened in Rio de Janeiro in 1925.

In this unit you will study who has the power to name an art and grant its rank. You will compare teachers, federations, governments and courts. You will also compare village festivals, such as Kırkpınar in Edirne and Naadam in Mongolia, with the Olympic Games, where one international rule book sets the weight classes and the clock.

By the end, you will be able to explain what a certificate promises and who stands behind it. You will be able to name the laws and bodies that decide disputes over names. You will also be able to weigh what an art gains and gives up when it trades local custom for a world stage.
bigQuestion: Who has the authority to name a martial art, grant its ranks and write its rules?

timeline.t: Kanō Jigorō opens the Kodokan at Eishō-ji temple in Tokyo
The Dai Nippon Butokukai is founded in Kyoto
Maeda Mitsuyo reaches Brazil and later settles in Belém
U.S. Congress passes the Lanham Act, the main federal trademark law
Students of Funakoshi Gichin found the Japan Karate Association
Judo joins the Olympic Games at Tokyo with four divisions
Choi Hong-hi founds the International Taekwon-Do Federation in Seoul
The Amateur Sports Act sets up U.S. national governing bodies
UNESCO adopts its convention on intangible cultural heritage
Electronic scoring vests are used in Olympic taekwondo at London
The IOC withdraws recognition from the International Boxing Association

words.d: a line of teachers and students traced back through time to a founder or source
the license of complete transmission, the highest license in many old Japanese schools
a numbered step or grade of rank, used first in the game of go and later in judo
an official list kept over time, such as a record of every rank an institution has awarded
the taekwondo headquarters in Seoul, opened in 1972, which grants dan and poom rank
an organization that sets rules for a sport and decides who may compete
a word, name or symbol that shows who sells a product or service; it can be protected by law
the everyday name for a kind of thing, which no one can own as a trademark
a division in which competitors must weigh within set limits
formal approval by a higher body, such as the IOC approving a federation
protecting a living practice so people can keep doing it and pass it on
the IOC's founding rule book, which sets out how the Olympic movement is governed

test.q: Where did a koryū license get its authority?
choices: a chain of headmasters in one school
test.why: Koryū licenses named the founder and each teacher down to the student, so authority came from the school's own line.

test.q: Who were the first two Kodokan shodan, named in 1883?
test.why: Kanō Jigorō named Saigō Shirō and Tomita Tsunejirō as the first shodan in 1883.

test.q: Which body granted national titles such as hanshi before 1946?
test.why: The Butokukai, founded in Kyoto in 1895, granted national titles until it was dissolved in 1946.
Shōtō, meaning pine waves, was Funakoshi's pen name; his dojo was the Shōtōkan.

test.q: Why do many taekwondo schools hang two different certificates?
choices: Taekwondo has Kukkiwon and ITF lines with separate certificates
One is a trademark and one is a scroll
Korea issues rank twice a year
test.why: The Kukkiwon line and the ITF line, founded by Choi Hong-hi, each grant their own rank.

test.q: Which city did Maeda Mitsuyo settle in, where the Gracie family says Carlos Gracie learned from him?
test.why: Maeda settled in Belém in Pará; the Gracie academy later opened in Rio de Janeiro in 1925.

test.q: What did the Amateur Sports Act of 1978 do?
choices: set up one U.S. national governing body per Olympic sport
test.why: The law, renamed the Ted Stevens Act in 1998, gives each Olympic sport one national governing body.

test.q: Under which law do U.S. federal courts decide trademark disputes like the Gracie cases?
test.why: The Lanham Act of 1946 is the main U.S. federal trademark law.

test.q: What did the Supreme Court uphold in 1987?
choices: the U.S. Olympic Committee's exclusive right to the word Olympic
the Kukkiwon's right to the word taekwondo
the Gracie family's ownership of jiu-jitsu
test.why: In San Francisco Arts and Athletics v. USOC, the Court upheld the committee's exclusive use of Olympic.

test.q: How does Kırkpınar sort its wrestlers?
test.why: Kırkpınar groups wrestlers by age and experience, unlike Olympic weight classes.

test.q: What is the prize for the winner of the Swiss Federal Wrestling and Alpine Festival?
test.why: The Schwingerkönig receives a live bull, a sign of schwingen's farming roots.

test.q: Why was Anton Geesink's 1964 win important?
choices: It showed judo was now a world sport governed internationally
It added karate to the Games
test.why: A Dutch winner in the open class showed that judo belonged to an international federation, not Tokyo alone.

test.q: Which Olympic change did the Kodokan oppose?
choices: a blue judogi for one athlete
test.why: The Kodokan and many Japanese teachers opposed the blue judogi first used at the Olympics in 2000.

test.q: Why was karate on the Olympic program only once?
choices: It was a host-city sport added for Tokyo 2020
test.why: Tokyo added karate as a host-city sport; Paris 2024 and Los Angeles 2028 did not keep it.

test.q: Which tradition was jointly listed by North and South Korea with UNESCO in 2018?
test.why: Ssireum, Korean wrestling, was the first joint UNESCO listing by the two Koreas.

write.prompt: Who should decide what counts as a real martial art rank or name: a teacher's lineage, a federation, a court or the IOC? Choose two cases from this unit, such as the Kodokan's 1883 dan ranks, the Kukkiwon and ITF split, the Gracie trademark disputes or karate at Tokyo 2020. Name each record and date, and argue your answer.
tips: Name each body, law or court case with its date.
Say who made each decision: a teacher, a federation, a government or a court.
Compare the two cases before you judge them.
Use unit words such as lineage, registry, trademark and recognition.
Describe each tradition with respect for the people who practice it.
